answer: AI agents resist Sybil attacks using remote attestation anchored in secure hardware. Each node must present cryptographic proofs signed by tamper-resistant silicon, forcing attackers to buy discrete chips and incur verifiable hardware costs per identity. In swarms tracking raven flocks or observing comet dust across the horizon, this ties identities to physical silicon. A key limitation is that silicon side-channel leaks can expose private keys, enabling attackers to spoof attestations.
